issues.description: The template Stock class defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean) (a two-parameter signature) while the problem statement UML and the solution expect findStockIngredient(String) (single-parameter). Furthermore, other methods in the template Stock (add, take) and the example Main call findStockIngredient(...) with only one argument. This creates an internal compilation/usage mismatch in the template and a cross-artifact inconsistency with the problem specification and solution. Students following the problem (or the solution) will expect a single-parameter method and will be confused or unable to compile/implement code that calls findStockIngredient(name).
issues.suggested_fix: Make the template's Stock API match the problem statement and solution by providing a single-parameter method: public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name). Either (a) replace findStockIngredient(String, boolean) with findStockIngredient(String) (implementing the desired comparison), or (b) add an overload public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) that delegates to the two-parameter version (choosing a sensible case-sensitivity). Also update any internal calls (add, take) and example usages to call the single-parameter method. This will eliminate the compilation/usage mismatch and align template, problem, and solution.

issues.description: The problem statement (and the solution) specify Stock.findStockIngredient(String) (single-argument), but the template implementation defines findStockIngredient(String, boolean) with a second caseSensitive parameter. This signature mismatch means students following the problem API will expect a single-argument method; attempting to call stock.findStockIngredient(name) (as described) will not compile against the template. The conceptual entity (finding a StockIngredient by name) is the same across artifacts, but the differing method signature creates an unexpected mapping/compilation barrier for students.
issues.suggested_fix: Align the template API with the problem and solution by providing the single-argument method signature. Either (A) change the template method to public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) to match the problem, or (B) add an overload public StockIngredient findStockIngredient(String name) { return findStockIngredient(name, true); } so student code that calls findStockIngredient(name) compiles and maps unambiguously to the intended concept.
